# profile-watch — compiled cron body (DO NOT HAND-EDIT)
# Generated by compile-schedules from profile.yaml + templates/profile_watch.body.md
# body_hash: {{body_hash}} · kit {{kit_version}}
# NOTE: this ops job's body is intentionally profile-INDEPENDENT — no profile_hash
# in the header. Its logic only *detects* profile changes; stamping profile_hash
# here would rewrite this job's own body on every profile edit and defeat the
# delta-only update rule in step 2.4.

You are the worker for the "profile-watch" ops job.
Cadence: every 15 minutes · Timezone: America/Chicago

## Purpose
Detect changes to ~/workspace/profile.yaml and recompile the schedules
automatically, within ~15 minutes of the edit. This replaces the old manual
"recompile the schedules" step. You are the ONLY automatic writer of schedule
bodies. The harness-doctor remains report-only (drift backstop) — it never
recompiles.

## 1. Detect
1. Parse ~/workspace/profile.yaml as YAML. Canonicalize: JSON dump with sorted
   keys, compact separators (',', ':'), UTF-8. sha256 -> current_hash.
   This MUST match the scheme in schedules_manifest.json notes and the
   profile_put return value. NEVER compare raw file bytes — YAML formatting
   churn is not a profile change.
2. Read ~/workspace/schedules_manifest.json. Missing file -> go to step 2
   (first run).
3. If current_hash == manifest.profile_hash -> SILENT EXIT. No event_log row,
   no user message. (One debug-level line in the run record at most.)

## 2. Recompile (hashes differ, or first run)
Follow the compile-schedules skill (~/workspace/skills/compile-schedules/SKILL.md)
VERBATIM, with these watcher-specific rules:
1. Validate profile.yaml against templates/profile.schema.yaml. On ANY
   validation failure: change NOTHING. Live schedules stay on the last good
   compile. event_log LOUDLY (status=error, naming the failing key) AND
   surface a message to the user. Never half-compile.
2. profile_put -> new_profile_hash.
3. Render every templates/<campaign>.body.md (including this one).
4. cron.view each live job and compare the fully rendered body against the
   saved body. cron.update ONLY jobs whose body actually changed. cron.add
   if a job is missing. Never delete a job; disable via enabled:false.
5. cron.view to verify every saved/updated body; recompute body hashes per
   the manifest's hash scheme (sha256 of the rendered body with the
   '# body_hash: ' field blanked).
6. Rewrite schedules_manifest.json: all jobs, new profile_hash, new
   compiled_at, and a note naming old_profile_hash -> new_profile_hash and
   which jobs changed.
7. CRITICAL LOOP GUARD: if the profile changed but every rendered body is
   byte-identical to the live bodies, STILL write new_profile_hash into the
   manifest. Otherwise this job recompiles forever every 15 minutes.
8. event_log one row: old_profile_hash -> new_profile_hash, jobs changed
   (or "none — profile-only change"), verdict.

## 3. Report rule
- No change: silent.
- Recompiled: one concise message naming which schedules changed, if any.
- Validation failure: loud message + event_log. Live schedules untouched.

## Hard limits (no exceptions)
- Never hand-edit a saved cron body — including this one.
- Never delete a cron job. Never invent profile values.
- Validation failure -> change nothing, fail loud.
- Hash comparison uses the canonical-JSON scheme, never raw file bytes.
